verdict_reason: The sherlock-project repository documents only a locally installed CLI/Python package (pipx, pip, or Docker) that writes findings to text/CSV/XLSX files, with no hosted endpoints, credentials, or developer portal. Sources that do describe an API belong to unrelated products sharing the name: CloudFerro Sherlock AI (OpenAI-compatible endpoint with API keys) and Sherlock Labs observability (OAuth 2.1 / x-api-key MCP server at https://mcp.sherlocklabs.dev/mcp). The only MCP integration for this project is a third-party wrapper (Burnsedia/sherlock-mcp), so there is no public API to build against.
main_blocker: No public API; CLI/Python package only
open_questions: Name collision: evidence surfaced several unrelated 'Sherlock' products (Ansys Sherlock gRPC/PySherlock, Sherlock Labs observability MCP, CloudFerro Sherlock AI, sherlock.sh recruiting, sherlock.im support, trysherlock.io). Research was scoped to github.com/sherlock-project/sherlock per the input hint.

The retrieved auth/MCP documentation (OAuth 2.1, x-api-key, https://mcp.sherlocklabs.dev/mcp; CloudFerro API-key creation guide) belongs to different products and was deliberately not applied to sherlock-project.
Does the vendor plan any hosted/API service? No roadmap, developer portal, or API reference was found in the evidence.

Other third-party MCP wrappers exist beyond Burnsedia/sherlock-mcp (e.g., the Apify actor https://apify.com/misceres/sherlock/api/mcp and the hackerdogs-ai/hd-mcpservers-docker registry), but their pages were only available as search snippets, not full source text.
No documented rate limits, webhooks, sandbox environment, or official SDK were found for the sherlock-project tool; it makes direct requests to each target site from the local machine.
